cf.title: Avoid unnecessary StringInfo allocation in tablesync COPY buffer

input.subject: Avoid unnecessary StringInfo allocation in tablesync COPY buffer

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The change is a refactoring of one file, tablesync.c, with no user-visible surface. P20 does not carry over, because v3 uses initReadOnlyStringInfo(), which is meant for buffers that are not NUL-terminated. The open point is a choice of form between v2 (CopyBuf struct) and v3 (read-only StringInfoData), which Álvaro Herrera has not yet answered.

brief.title: Avoid StringInfo allocation for the tablesync COPY buffer
brief.problem: In tablesync.c, copy_table() allocates copybuf with makeStringInfo(), but copy_read_data() uses it only to hold a data pointer, length and cursor. The allocated buffer is never used, because walrcv_receive() supplies the data. The thread names no user-facing problem; this is a code cleanup.
brief.proposed_design: v1 replaces the heap allocation with a static StringInfoData that is reset before COPY starts. v2 used a small file-local CopyBuf struct instead, after Álvaro Herrera called the StringInfo use a misuse. v3, by Zizhuan Liu, makes copybuf a function-scope static StringInfoData in copy_read_data() and wraps each received buffer with initReadOnlyStringInfo().
author_claims: The buffer from makeStringInfo() is never used, so both allocations can go.
The change follows earlier cleanups that prefer stack-allocated StringInfoData, such as commit a63bbc811d41.
Denis Smirnov expects no measurable performance difference between v1 and v2.
v3 keeps the existing handling of leftover unconsumed data across calls.
Read-only StringInfoData via initReadOnlyStringInfo() is an established pattern in walreceiver.c, logical/worker.c and other files.
brief.thread_state: Álvaro Herrera objected to v1, Chao Li answered with v2, and Denis Smirnov argued for v1 with initReadOnlyStringInfo(). Zizhuan Liu, a listed reviewer, posted v3 on that line; neither Álvaro nor Chao Li has replied to v3.
unclear: The material does not show a commit message or file list for v3.
Álvaro Herrera has not said whether read-only StringInfoData answers his objection.
Chao Li has not said whether v3 replaces his own patch.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which version is now proposed for commit: v2 with the file-local CopyBuf struct, or v3 with a read-only StringInfoData?
Does wrapping each received buffer with initReadOnlyStringInfo() answer the "misuse of the StringInfo abstraction" concern from message #2?
Is the static copybuf in v3 reset before each COPY, including when one worker syncs a second table?
Will v3 get a commit message that explains why a static variable is used and how leftover data survives between calls?

committability.owner_note: Álvaro Herrera objected to v1 in message #2 but has not replied to v3. A committer who knows the logical replication tablesync code would have to pick between v2 and v3.
committability.liability: Small: one function's buffer state in tablesync.c. The owner signs that leftover COPY data and the static state behave as before in every tablesync worker.
committability.author_follow_up: Chao Li posted v2 two days after the objection in message #2. The thread shows no reply from him to v3.

priority.reason: The patch is under 3 KiB, touches only tablesync.c and benefits the people who maintain that file. It has waited through three CommitFests for agreement on v2 or v3, which one reply from the objecting committer could settle.

provisional_note: The code was not read, and v3 has no commit message or file list in the material. Whether v3 resets the static copybuf before each COPY and keeps leftover data valid between calls could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix and improve allocation formulas
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Andres Freund, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set fixes two allocation size formulas found with a coccinelle script, in btree_gist and pg_verifybackup. A second, 277kB generated patch rewrites palloc(sizeof(T) * count) calls across the tree as palloc(sizeof(*var) * count), so the size follows the variable's type.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Michael Paquier opposed sizeof(*var) as the preferred style, because it hides what is being allocated and a typo like sizeof(*bar) goes undetected, while palloc_object()/palloc_array() let the compiler catch type mismatches. Andres Freund objected to a mass change for its backpatch hazard and review cost, and said the style should be agreed and documented first. Of the two formula fixes, Michael Paquier committed the btree_gist one as 5cf03552fbb4, merged with a fix from another thread, and left the pg_verifybackup uint8-vs-char change for others to comment on.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: IMO what it mostly accomplishes is to remove a cue as to what we are allocating.

precedents_retrieved.title: tablesync early exit
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes a tablesync worker call process_syncing_tables() before it enters the apply main loop, so a worker with nothing left to do exits early. The author presented it as a small optimization and as a cleaner split of work between tablesync and apply workers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila objected that exiting before the tablesync worker receives any message skips changes up to the LSN where the copy finished. That is safe with the current code but would lose changes for the table in a design where the apply worker applies streamed in-progress transactions, which had already been proposed on -hackers. The saving was only the work to receive messages for one transaction, so the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As per my understanding, this is safe as per the current code but it
can't be guaranteed for future implementations and the amount of extra
work is additional work to receive the messages for one transaction.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add the ability to limit the amount of memory that can be allocated to backends.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch tracks the memory each backend allocates and shows it in pg_stat_activity, and a second patch adds max_total_backend_memory to cap total backend allocations across the cluster. A later version by John Morris keeps local counters in each process and adds them to shared counters from time to time, with error of up to 1 MB per process.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message shown is a code review from September 2023, and no message covers the 2024 decision. Earlier messages object to widening pg_stat_activity and note that the counts miss OS memory and direct malloc() calls, but nothing shown ties these points to the outcome.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve monitoring of shared memory allocations
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_shmem_allocations show the full size of shared hash tables by allocating the header, directory, segments and elements in one ShmemInitStruct() call in hash_create(). It also replaces most ShmemAlloc() calls with named ShmemInitStruct() allocations so they are tracked.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The first two parts were committed and then reverted after a bug in non-shared hash tables: dir_realloc() freed a directory that was no longer allocated on its own, which caused a pfree error. Tomas Vondra did not push the fix for shared hash tables only into PG18, because dynahash is critical and its tests never run dir_realloc(). He and Amit Kapila asked for better test coverage first. The author did not add the tests, and Heikki Linnakangas later closed the entry as superseded by commit 9fe9ecd516.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This was superseded by commit 9fe9ecd516, I'll close this in the commitfest app.

precedents_retrieved.title: pre-allocating WAL files
precedents_retrieved.summary: Pre-create WAL segment files ahead of need so that backends do not wait for new 16 MB segments to be zero-filled during write-heavy load. The patch first used a separate WAL allocator process and later moved pre-allocation into the checkpointer.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after more than a year because he saw very little interest in the feature. Reviewers found the code acceptable, but their benchmarks showed little or no performance gain, and one reviewer doubted it was worth the effort. Bharath Rupireddy asked whether fallocate would make pre-allocation unnecessary and asked for timing numbers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's now been over a year since I first posted a patch in this thread, and
I still sense very little interest for this feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add function to release an allocated SQLDA
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an ecpg function, ECPGfreeSQLDA(), that frees an SQLDA chain such as the one that FETCH ALL into a descriptor returns. It gives applications a library call for this so they do not have to free each SQLDA with the C library's free(), which Windows users cannot safely use.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. Thomas Munro asked for two functions, one to free a single SQLDA (to back-patch as a Windows fix) and one to free the whole chain, and asked to fix mismatched function names. Later the patch no longer applied to master, and Dmitry Dolgov closed the entry when no new version came.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Due to lack of response I'm marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize memory allocation in function "bringetbitmap"
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes bringetbitmap so that the BRIN tuple and the BrinMemTuple arrays are allocated once before the loop over page ranges, so the loop no longer allocates them for every range. Following Alvaro Herrera's suggestion, brin_deform_tuple gets an optional BrinMemTuple argument to reuse, and brin_new_memtuple allocates the values/allnulls/hasnulls arrays.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra's review found several problems in the revised patch. The fixed size estimate for btup ignores palloc chunk sizes and is never raised, and brin_new_memtuple no longer initializes the tuple, which breaks its documented contract. The author did not reply to the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So I think this is wrong and needs to be reverted.

precedents_retrieved.title: A infrastructure to detect misuse of spin lock easier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started with a proposal to make s_lock_stuck a WARNING in production builds instead of a PANIC. It became an assert-build mechanism that tracks whether a spinlock or buffer header lock is held and fails when code holding one calls errstart, waits for an LWLock, or takes another spinlock.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Andres Freund raised API and performance concerns on v9, and the last visible message is Andy Fan posting v10 in reply, with no later review shown before the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024.

roaster_notes.note: The only related precedent, P20, was reverted because a StringInfo pointed at a buffer that was not NUL-terminated. v3 uses initReadOnlyStringInfo(), which exists for that case, so the reason does not carry over. Álvaro's "misuse" objection (message #2) is still open on v3, but it is a design-taste question that no precedent decides.

The change is internal to tablesync.c and has no user-facing surface: no syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump, psql or client-visible behaviour. Nothing in the standards and compatibility angle applies. P20 is about NUL termination in read-only StringInfo, which is an implementation concern outside this angle.

The change only touches how the tablesync worker holds received COPY data in its own memory. It adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, protocol or exported API change, so nothing crosses a process or version boundary. Without the code, I could not check whether the static copybuf state is reset if a worker ever syncs a second table.

The patch changes only how copy_read_data() in tablesync.c keeps its pointer, length and cursor. It adds no privilege, role, setting, view, error text or user-reachable path, and the COPY data comes from the publisher as before. The tablesync worker's trust in that data does not change, so there is no security or privilege angle to raise.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is no objection. All three versions change one file, add no hot-path cost, GUC or API, and v3 reuses initReadOnlyStringInfo(), which already has many callers in the tree, including worker.c and walreceiver.c. [P20] does not apply, because initReadOnlyStringInfo() was added for buffers that are not NUL-terminated. The thread still needs Álvaro Herrera's answer to v3. Without the code I could not check whether v3 still clears copybuf before each COPY, as v1 did.

This is an internal cleanup with no user-facing feature, so no existing feature or extension can replace it. v3 reuses initReadOnlyStringInfo() and drops v2's separate CopyBuf struct, which settles the duplicate-mechanism concern from message #3. [P20] concerned NUL termination, and initReadOnlyStringInfo() is meant for non-NUL-terminated buffers, so that precedent does not apply.

This is a refactoring-only cleanup, so a lack of user demand is not a reason to reject it. Its users are the people who maintain tablesync.c. Álvaro Herrera and Denis Smirnov both engaged on how the code should look, and the cost to everyone else is close to zero because nothing user-visible changes.
